sources.note: Replaces PPO's scalar mean-squared-error critic head with a categorical predictor over a discretized value support trained by cross-entropy against Gaussian-smoothed targets, decodes it back to a scalar for an unchanged GAE update, and shows the resulting critic is better calibrated and produces near-symmetric advantages where the MSE critic penalizes failures two-to-three times harder than it rewards successes.
sources.title: Start Classifying: Categorical Critics for LLM Reinforcement Learning

sources.note: Formalizes test-time scaling as budgeted inference over a model's implicit prefix tree, separates three structurally different regimes that a single scalar budget conflates, specifies what a reproducible inference protocol must declare, and releases 1.9 million traces — with the empirical section showing a selection score that makes accuracy fall from 75.56% to 65.83% as the candidate bank grows.
sources.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility

sources.note: A training-free two-stage prompting protocol that extracts a problem's answer-space constraints first and then checks its own intermediate and final results against them, routed on by a regex detector.
sources.title: Constraint-First Reasoning: A Training-Free Protocol for Exploiting Answer-Space Constraints in Mathematical Problem Solving

sources.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
sources.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

result.definition: A competition mathematics set used across 4 sources as one of the newer small benchmarks in test-time-scaling and distillation suites, alongside HMMT and CMIMC. Its role is the same as the other thirty-problem competition sets: it is where methods separate and where the separation is weakest in evidence, so intervals rather than point estimates are what the archive should read from it. None of the sources describes its construction.
